title: Moving away from a settling point is felt as unpleasure, moving back as pleasure

statements.text: Deviation away from a homeostatic settling point, rising uncertainty, is felt as unpleasure, and returning toward it, falling uncertainty, is felt as pleasure. The settling point itself resolves the affect, so affect in general registers continued need. There are many kinds of pleasure and unpleasure, and the kind identifies the need at issue.

sources.quote: deviation away from a homeostatic settling point (increasing uncertainty) is felt as unpleasure
The settling point itself (‘satiation’) resolves the affect
